cells.tense: You are here with a clear sense of which way to point, and the clearing is under way.
cells.act: share your strength where it is needed
cells.ask: Name the ending you have kept quiet about finishing. Give the person inside it the honest piece of help they are owed from you, do your part, and stop before it turns into running them.
cells.core:
You know which way you are pointed, and you are taking apart what has finished with a steady hand. Nothing gets dragged out and nothing is torn down for show; the ending gets made, and the people near it can stand on solid ground while things move around them. That steadiness is not just temperament. Something in you holds and releases without gripping either one.

Attention is what pays for it. Someone in the clearing needs help you have not given yet — a short honest word, one piece of work finished for them. Give it this week and then step out of it. If you are wrong and the direction shifts, you have still closed one thing fully and unblocked one person. The way through stays open as long as you hold your end and let theirs stay theirs.
cells.sheetLine: You end things without breaking what has to keep living.
cells.verb: choosing which light to steer by and pointing the self at it
cells.place: in the middle of endings, clearing what has finished so something else can start

cells.tense: You will be braced for a future that cannot be written in, so the endings keep getting put off.
cells.act: list the pulls on you and mark which are yours
cells.ask: Put everything pulling on you onto one page in twenty minutes. Mark the ones you actually chose. Take one that is not yours and stop feeding it your hours, just for this week.
cells.core:
The direction is set, but you are already living past the ending — rehearsing what comes after, keeping every door an option so none gets closed. From outside it looks like momentum. From where you stand, the clearing keeps not finishing because you keep adding to it. What is doing the steering has run past the moment it is actually in.

A fuller picture is not the fix; knowing which pulls are yours is. Put them all on paper and mark what you chose, then let one borrowed thing go for a week. Some of it will not come back, and that is the part doing the work. If the read is wrong, you have still sorted your week and turned your own eye on it.

cells.tense: You were standing at a door that has already closed behind you, and you have not turned around.
cells.act: take pleasure in the grown thing
cells.ask: Sit with one thing your life lately actually produced — a finished piece of work, a bond that held, something you kept alive — and spend ten minutes enjoying what it already is. No repairs, no inventory.
cells.core:
The ending happened without you; that is what is hard to see from where you stand. Something finished, and you have gone on treating it as unfinished, or avoiding any honest account of it. The direction is still there, but it points backward, held at a closed door. Nothing gets cleared while it is attended to that way.

What refills this is not effort. It is pleasure. There is something in your recent life that actually grew, and you have not let yourself enjoy it. Ten quiet minutes with it, nothing to fix. If this misreads where you are stuck, the act still costs nothing and shows you what you already have. Direction comes back the same way — by noticing what is real.
cells.sheetLine: You can't point forward from a door that's already closed.
cells.verb: choosing which light to steer by and pointing the self at it

cells.tense: You are steering this ending without having put your name on the choice, and someone else may be carrying it.
cells.act: give a concrete piece of help and finish it
cells.ask: Before the next thing you do for someone in this ending, say plainly that you picked it. Then finish the help you were already going to give and hand it over. The rest is theirs now.
cells.core:
You keep moving toward what matters and taking down what is in the way, and it works — help gets given, the ending gets made. What is missing is that the picking does not feel like yours. Somewhere it got filed under circumstance, or under what was needed, and you have been standing beside your own decisions. Nothing has been lost. You have just stopped being visible in it.

What brings you back into view is smaller than it sounds. Before the next helpful act, say out loud that you chose this. Not an apology and not a claim — the plain fact, once. Then finish what you were going to hand over and pass it along. If things move somewhere else afterward, nothing is wasted; they have seen what your word stands for.

attempts.check: The one unsupported claim is that a star has been picked and is being worked by real aspiration; the record only says the capacity for decisive direction exists, so where the person's own account is that no direction ever got chosen, the read lands on the wrong side and the reader can say so plainly. The asks survive that: each act is small, self-contained, and teaches something about what the person actually wants, working as well if they are still at the door as if they already went through it. The sentence that serves me more than them is 'the choice was already made' — it flatters the reading's internal logic and would tell the person what to think of themselves; it gets cut. Too Much and Too Little are written as opposite failures of the same capacity: tying the ending to a future outcome, versus still standing at an ending that already happened and cleaning nothing.
